scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Independent Instant Messages EN/B2 source-based test proposal; pending teacher approval.

tabs.title: Digital Signals
tabs.description: Analyse how users interpret short messages.

questions.q: Why can a brief 'OK.' cause an argument even when no offence is intended?
choices: Short messages always express irritation.
Text does not convey the context and non-verbal signals available in speech.
Every recipient interprets punctuation in the same way.
Typing quickly necessarily changes what the sender means.
questions.explanation: The introduction attributes the misunderstanding to lost vocal and visual context.

questions.q: What does the full stop example reveal about texting conventions?
choices: Punctuation is never appropriate in personal messages.
Older relatives intentionally use full stops to signal anger.
Young users cannot recognise a grammatically correct sentence.
The same form can carry different social meanings for different generations.
questions.explanation: The writer contrasts younger and older interpretations of punctuation.

questions.q: Why might a delayed reply be unfairly interpreted as indifference?
choices: The recipient does not know what prevented the sender from responding earlier.
Only deliberately rude people reply after several hours.
A slow message is always more formal than a fast one.
Messages sent during lessons automatically change their wording.
questions.explanation: The writer notes that work or lessons can explain response time.

questions.q: What assumption causes Dana to begin looking for another farewell present?
choices: Marek has explicitly rejected every photo book.
The teacher has requested a different present.
She mistakes Marek's brief agreement for opposition to her suggestion.
Dana discovers that all photo books are sold out.
questions.explanation: Dana reads 'fine' as negative although Marek meant approval.

questions.q: Why is the group's lost time important to the author's argument?
choices: Group chats never help people make decisions.
An ambiguous message can lead to unnecessary actions and delays.
Farewell presents are difficult to buy online.
Marek should have ordered the book before receiving a suggestion.
questions.explanation: The example shows how assumptions create practical consequences.

questions.q: Why does the writer reject the idea that friends should always send long formal messages?
choices: Long messages cannot be sent in group chats.
Formal writing is grammatically impossible on phones.
Friends never need to discuss serious topics.
Overly formal wording may itself create an unfamiliar and misleading tone.
questions.explanation: The fourth paragraph says formality may feel strange and cause further misunderstanding.

questions.q: When is adding a few words particularly valuable?
choices: When a reply involves a decision, disagreement or another person's feelings.
Whenever a friend sends a picture of food.
Only when messaging an older relative.
Whenever the sender wants to avoid speaking in person.
questions.explanation: The author recommends clarification when the stakes of interpretation rise.

questions.q: What advantage does asking 'Did you mean...?' have over silent withdrawal?
choices: It guarantees that the other person will agree.
It proves the initial message was rude.
It checks intention before the misunderstanding grows.
It makes a voice call unnecessary in every case.
questions.explanation: The closing paragraph advises asking rather than assuming.

questions.q: Why might a friend group agree on the meaning of a thumbs-up reaction?
choices: It makes every difficult conversation unnecessary.
It prevents people from using punctuation.
It ensures that everyone is always available.
A shared convention reduces uncertainty about whether someone will respond later.
questions.explanation: The author describes explicit shared signals as a way to remove doubt.

questions.q: Which conversation would most benefit from moving to a call?
choices: Choosing the colour of a simple emoji.
A sensitive disagreement in which short replies are being misunderstood.
Sending a familiar address to a friend.
Confirming that a photograph has arrived.
questions.explanation: The ending advocates richer communication when a topic becomes complex or emotional.
